column1: # Japanese cues of an utterance, read by the register model (R). Stand-in for the cue summary that S and L
# will provide (Utterance.sourceLevel, Clause.polite, Clause.jreg): until then R scans the source text with
# these rows. A cue fires when one of its rows matches.
#   cue     polite (desu/masu at a sentence end), polite-any (desu/masu anywhere), keigo (尊敬語/謙譲語),
#           set (formal set phrases), archaic (old speech), stiff (stiff plain speech), casual (plain endings),
#           first:<name> (first-person pronoun), tail (a sentence-final particle stripped before `end` rows),
#           quotative (a string after which an any-not-quoted match does not count)
#   mode    tail rows: strong marks a particle that makes an unbracketed line speech (inner monologue ending
#           in よ/ね/ぞ is 해, not narration -다: 82% of 294 dev lines); other rows:
#           end: the last sentence ends in text, after any number of tail particles and closing marks;
#           any: text anywhere in the utterance; any-not-quoted: anywhere, unless a quotative follows it
#   notafter  characters that must not come right before text (the ます of ぶちかます is not polite)
